questions.question: The Planning Commission of India was replaced by NITI Aayog in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The Planning Commission was charged with the responsibility of making assessments of all resources of the country, augmenting deficient resources, formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources, and determining priorities.
 
• On 1 January 2015__, a Cabinet resolution was passed to replace the Planning Commission with the newly formed NITI Aayog.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• NITI-National Institution for Transforming India

 
 
• NITI Aayog is a policy think tank of the Government of India which replaced the Planning Commission of India. It was established with the aim of achieving sustainable development goals with cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of State Governments in economic policies.
 
• One of the objectives of NITI Aayog is to develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate these progressively at higher levels of government.
 
• Chairman of NITI Aayog- PM Narendra Modi

questions.question: Who was the first female Muslim ruler of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Razia Sultana.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Razia Sultana was the first female Muslim ruler of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• She ruled in Delhi from 1236 to 1240 as the Sultan herself – it was a title never before bestowed on a woman, a position of power never before attained by a woman.
 
• Before ascending to the throne of Delhi after her father’s death, the reign was briefly handed over to her half-brother Rukn ud-din Firuz.
 
• But after Firuz’s assassination within 6 months of his ascendency, the nobles agreed to place Razia on the throne.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Slave Dynasty __

 
• Established by Qutb ud-Din Aibak.
 
• Dynasty lasted from 1206 to 1290.
 
• It was the first of the dynasties to rule as the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Dynasty ended when Jalal ud din Firuz Khilji overthrew the last Mamluk ruler Muiz ud din Qaiqabad in 1290.
 
• Dynasty was succeeded by the Khilji (or Khalji) dynasty, the second dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: As of 2022 , India is the ______ largest economy in the world (as measured by nominal GDP).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F**____**ifth**__.​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• On the basis of nominal GDP, India is the world's fifth-largest economy as of 2022.
 
• GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product.
 
• GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced during a given time period within a nation's domestic borders.
 
• GDP is the most referred indicator for highlighting a country's economy, whether its size or its performance, and GDP is used as the benchmark growth indicator.
 
• The major contribution of GDP in India is of the service sector, followed by the manufacturing sector, and then by the primary sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GDP:

 
 
• GDP’s full form is Gross Domestic Product is evaluated regularly to account for changing production structure, relative prices, and better recording of economic activities.
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total monetary value of final goods and services produced in the economic territories of a country in a given year. 
 
• Non-monetary goods and services (e.g. cooking by housewives) are not included in GDP calculation. 
 
• Economic transactions virtually include everything economic in the country. For e.g., if a stockbroker sells and purchases the same stock worth Rs. 1000 five times in a day, it does not increase the GDP of the country by Rs. 5000.
 
• Economic transactions may also include buying and selling of bonds, FII inflows, and outflows, etc. 
 
• GDP includes the value of all goods and services produced within a country within a year.

questions.question: Raman wants to use a rear-view mirror in his vehicle. Which type of mirror should he pick for it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Convex ____**Mirrors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**** ****Convex mirror:**

__
 
• The **spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is in upside is called a convex mirror.
 
• It is always from a virtual image of any object.
 
• It is used as a rear-view mirror in the vehicle
 
• It is also from a full-size diminished image of the objects placed at far away distances with a wide range of field of; view.
 
• Due to a wide range of fields of view, we can see the image of the maximum object behind the vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The optical instrument which reflects the light falling on it and makes images of anybody is called a mirror.
 
• A mirror that has a spherical reflecting surface is called a spherical mirror.
 
• A mirror whose reflecting surface is flat is called a plane mirror.
 
• A mirror whose reflecting surface is part of a cylindrical surface is called a cylindrical mirror.

questions.question: When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **12 August 2009**, the first draft of the **Direct Tax Code Bill **was created.
 
• **In 2010, a Revised Discussion Paper was created.**
 
• **In 2010, The Direct Tax Code bill was introduced in Parliament,** and a Standing Committee of Finance (SCF) was appointed for a detailed discussion.
 
• In 2012, the committee submitted its report to Parliament.
 
• In 2014, a revised version of the Direct Tax Code was created after the committee report.
 
• The bill lapsed due to the change in government after the general elections.
 
• **In 2017**, An expert committee was set up to draft a fresh Direct Tax Code.
 
• In Aug 2019, the task force report was submitted to the Finance Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Tax Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Income Tax
 A tax on the income earned by individuals, HUFs, companies, and other entities.
 
 

 Goods and Services Tax (GST)
 A value-added tax on the supply of goods and services, which replaced several indirect taxes such as excise duty, VAT, and service tax.
 
 

 Corporate Tax
 A tax on the profits earned by companies and other business entities.
 
 

 Capital Gains Tax
 A tax on the profits earned from the sale of capital assets such as property, shares, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Wealth Tax
 A tax on the net wealth of individuals and HUFs, which was abolished in 2015.
 
 

 Customs Duty
 A tax on the import and export of goods across India's borders.
 
 

 Excise Duty
 A tax on the production and manufacture of goods within the country.
 
 

 Securities Transaction Tax (STT)
 A tax on the purchase and sale of securities such as stocks, bonds, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Professional Tax
 A tax on the income earned by professionals such as doctors, lawyers, and chartered accountants.
 
 

 Property Tax
 A tax on the ownership or occupation of property, which is levied by local authorities such as municipalities and panchayats.

questions.question: In India, palm, coconut, keora, agar are the common trees of which of the following forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Mangrove Forests**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Mangrove Forests

__
 
• Found in the areas of coasts influenced by tides. Mud and silt get accumulated on such coasts.
 
• Dense mangroves are the common varieties with roots of the plants submerged underwater.
 
• The deltas of the Ganga, the Mahanadi, the Krishana, the Godavari, and the Kaveri are covered by such vegetation.
 
• In the Ganga Brahmaputra delta, Sundari trees are found, which provide durable hard timber.
 
• Palm, coconut, keora, agar, also grow in some parts of the delta.
 
• Royal Bengal Tiger is the famous animal in these forests. Turtles, crocodiles, gharials, and snakes are also found in these forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__Tropical Evergreen Forests:__

 
• These forests are restricted to heavy rainfall areas of the *Western Ghats and the island groups of Lakshadweep, Andaman, and Nicobar, upper parts of Assam, and Tamil Nadu coast.*
 
• They are at their best in areas having more than 200 cm of rainfall with a short dry season.
 
• The trees reach great heights up to 60 meters or even above.
 
• Since the region is warm and wet throughout the year, it has luxuriant vegetation of all kinds.
 
• The trees, shrubs, and creepers give it a multilayered structure.
 
• There is no definite time for trees to shed their leaves.
 
• As such, these forests appear green all the year-round

Tropical Deciduous Forests

 
• ​These are the most widespread forests of India.
 
• They are also called the monsoon forests and spread over the region receiving rainfall between 200 cm and 70 cm.
 
• Trees of this forest type shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in dry summer.
 
• On the basis of the availability of water, these forests are further divided into moist and dry deciduous.

Natural vegetation refers to a plant community, which has grown naturally without human aid and has been left undisturbed by humans for a long time. The following major types of vegetation may be identified in our country

 
• Tropical Evergreen Forests
 
• Tropical Deciduous Forests
 
• Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs
 
• Montane Forests
 
• Mangrove Forests

questions.question: Somewhat before the time of Mauryan empire, about __________ years ago, emperors in China began building the Great Wall.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **2400**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Somewhat before the time of the **Mauryan empire**, about **2400** years ago, emperors in China began building the **Great Wall.**
 
• It was meant to protect the **northern frontier **of the empire from** pastoral people.**
 
• Additions to the wall were made over a **period of 2000 years **because the **frontiers of the empire kept shifting.**
 
• The wall is about **21,196** **km long** and is made of **stone and brick,** with a road along the top.
 
• Several thousand people worked to build the wall.
 
• There are **watch towers all along**, at distances of about **100-200 m.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** __Mauryan Empire__

 
• The Maurya dynasty (321–185 BC) was a powerful dynasty in ancient India.
 
• The Maurya dynasty ruled India for 137 years.
 
• The credit for its establishment is given to Chandragupta Maurya and his minister Chanakya (Kautilya).
 
• This empire started from the plains of the Ganges river (today's Bihar and Bengal) in the state of Magadha in the east.
 
• Its capital was Pataliputra (near present-day Patna city).
 
• Chandragupta Maurya established this empire in 321 BC and rapidly expanded his empire towards the west.
 
• The Mauryan Empire grew and thrived during the Iron Age.
 
• He took advantage of the differences between several small regional kingdoms that had arisen after Alexander's invasion.
 
• By 316 BC, the Maurya dynasty had occupied the whole of North Western India.
 
• The Maurya dynasty expanded on a large scale in the reign of the Chakravarti emperor Ashoka.
 
• Due to Emperor Ashoka, the Maurya Empire became the greatest and most powerful and became famous all over the world.

questions.question: Who among the following was the architect of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Program (IGMDP) in India?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.*****__Key Points__** Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme

__
 
• IGMDP was the brainchild of renowned scientist Dr APJ Abdul Kalam.
 
• It was intended to attain self-sufficiency in the field of missile technology.
 
• After keeping in mind the requirements of various types of missiles by the defense forces, the program recognized the need to develop five missile systems.
 
• The IGMDP formally got the approval of the Indian government on 26th July 1983.
 
• The missiles developed under IGMDP are:
 
 
• Short-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile – Prithvi
 
• Intermediate-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile – Agni
 
• Short-range low-level surface-to-air missile – Trishul
 
• Medium-range surface-to-air missile – Akash
 
• Third-generation anti-tank missile – Nag
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Vikram Sarabhai:**

 
• Dr. Vikram Sarabhai was born on August 12, 1919, in Ahmadabad.
 
• Dr. Vikram Sarabhai was considered the Father of the Indian space *program.
 
• He was a great institution builder and established a large number of institutes in diverse fields.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad in November 1947.
 
• He was also Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission.
 
• Dr. Sarabhai's dialogue with NASA in 1966, the Satelite Instructional Television Experiment (SITE) was launched during July 1975-July 1976.
 
• Dr. Sarabhai started a project for the fabrication and launch of an Indian Satellite.
 
• As a result, the first Indian satellite, Aryabhata, was put in orbit in 1975 from a Russian Cosmodrome.
 
• He founded a Community Science Centre at Ahmedabad in 1966.
 
• Today, the Centre is called the Vikram A Sarabhai Community Science Centre.

**Homi J. Bhabha:**

 
• Homi J. Bhabha was an Indian nuclear physicist, founding director, and professor of physics at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. Colloquially known as the father of the Indian nuclear program.
 
• Homi J. Bhabha was the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission that was set-up in August 1948.
 
• Dr. Homi Bhabha established the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET) in January 1954.
 
• In 1966, Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay was renamed; Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC).
 
• Dr. Bhabha was one of the founding directors of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.
 
• He was awarded the Admas Prize.

questions.question: Chikungunya is an infection caused by _____ mosquito.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Aedes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chikungunya

 
 
• **Chikungunya** is a viral disease that is primarily transmitted to humans through the bite of infected mosquitoes. Here are some key points to understand about Chikungunya:
 
 
 
• **Cause:**
 
 
• Chikungunya is caused by the Chikungunya virus, which belongs to the alphavirus genus of the family Togaviridae. The primary vectors for Chikungunya are the Aedes species of mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, which are also responsible for transmitting diseases such as dengue and Zika.
 
 
 
• **Transmission: **
 
 
• **​**The Chikungunya virus is typically transmitted from human to human through the bite of an infected female mosquito. The mosquitoes typically bite during the day, with peak hours around dawn and dusk. Unlike some other mosquito-borne diseases, Chikungunya does not have an animal reservoir and primarily circulates among humans.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms: **
 
 
• **​**After an incubation period of 2 to 12 days, people infected with Chikungunya typically develop symptoms abruptly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Culex:**

 
• Culex mosquitoes are most commonly associated with the transmission of West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis, and St. Louis encephalitis.
 
• They typically breed in stagnant water and are often found in urban and suburban areas. Culex mosquitoes are generally most active during dusk and dawn.
 
• **Carrier**: Aedes mosquitoes (primarily Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus)

**Mansonia:**

 
• Mansonia mosquitoes are less well-known but can transmit diseases such as lymphatic filariasis.
 
• These mosquitoes breed in weedy swamps and marshes. They are unique in that their larvae and pupae attach to aquatic plants to obtain oxygen, rather than coming to the water’s surface.

**Anopheles:**

 
• Anopheles mosquitoes are best known for spreading malaria. They can also transmit other diseases such as lymphatic filariasis and some forms of encephalitis.
 
• Anopheles mosquitoes breed in clean, unpolluted water and are active primarily at night. They are distinguished by their characteristic resting posture, where their bodies are lifted at an angle to the surface.
 
• **Carrier:** Anopheles mosquitoes (primarily Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles funestus, among others)

questions.question: Aga Khan Palace is located in _____ city of Maharashtra.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Pune**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Aga Khan Palace was built by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III in the city of Pune, Maharashtra in 1892.
 
• The palace was an act of charity by the spiritual leader of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims, who wanted to help the poor in the neighboring areas of Pune, who were drastically hit by famine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Sir Sultan Mahomed Shah, Aga Khan III was the 48th Imam of the Nizari Ismaili sect of Islam.
 
• He played a very important role in giving the Muslims a political stance to express their opinions to the British.
 
• In 1906, the Aga Khan was a founding member and first president of the All India Muslim League.
